description: Agents need better data but buyers will not pay an independent exchange enough above direct APIs, subscriptions, or cloud marketplaces.
leading_indicator: Pilots generate usage but buyers refuse post-pilot markup or platform fee.
mitigation: Run only paid pilots with pre-agreed success metrics and renewal pricing; kill verticals that cannot support markup.

description: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Cloudflare, or Stripe absorbs the valuable layer before the exchange scales.
leading_indicator: Buyers ask to wait for native connectors, cloud listings, or model-platform source access.
mitigation: Build vertical workflow, licensing, audit, and outcome assets that can interoperate with platforms instead of competing only on infrastructure.

description: A publisher licenses content it does not own or cannot sublicense for AI retrieval, causing buyer claims and reputational collapse.
leading_indicator: Catalog contains wire content, freelancer work, UGC, images, or third-party datasets with unclear rights.
mitigation: Rights diligence, source-slice exclusions, warranties, indemnity, insurance pool, and audit of publisher rights.

description: The exchange pools nonpublic publisher price or revenue data and recommends prices in a RealPage-like pattern.
leading_indicator: Product requirements include optimal market pricing from competitor data or publisher price floors.
mitigation: Publisher-set prices only; no nonpublic cross-publisher pricing recommendations; antitrust counsel review.

failure_mode: Unfavorable legal rulings reduce licensing need
description: Courts bless market-substituting AI retrieval/training or user-delegated access, making unlicensed access look safe enough.
leading_indicator: Buyer counsel downgrades copyright/CFAA risk after Ross or Perplexity-style appellate rulings.
mitigation: Focus on quality, audit, indemnity, and SLAs where licensed access has value beyond legal risk.

description: CDNs/gateways enforce paid access at the edge and control publisher monetization before an independent exchange gains leverage.
leading_indicator: Publishers prefer Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, or AWS edge payment controls for all paid calls.
mitigation: Partner with edge providers; focus on demand-side workflow routing and vertical source quality.

description: Open MCP registries and source-published MCP servers make a proprietary catalog undifferentiated.
leading_indicator: Target sources publish free MCP metadata and buyers discover them through default registries.
mitigation: Treat MCP as adapter; differentiate with rights, settlement, audit, quality, and outcome data.

description: x402, MPP, Stripe, card, ACH, and cloud billing reduce payment handling to a commodity service.
leading_indicator: Buyers and publishers ask why the exchange charges beyond standard processor fees.
mitigation: Use payment partners and avoid positioning settlement as the moat; charge for licensing, QA, audit, and routing.

description: Premium rights holders publish APIs/MCP servers or sign direct AI/cloud deals, skimming the best supply from the exchange.
leading_indicator: Target publishers request only referral traffic or list elsewhere without exclusivity.
mitigation: Serve mid-tail specialized sources; offer onboarding, billing, and quality services that direct APIs lack.

description: Publishers list across multiple exchanges, clouds, and CDNs, forcing the platform fee down.
leading_indicator: Publishers compare channel fees and demand lower take rates or guarantees.
mitigation: Keep costs low; earn fees from workflow/audit value; avoid relying on exclusivity.

description: Buyers route only a subset of calls through the exchange and use existing subscriptions or direct APIs for the rest.
leading_indicator: Buyer source logs show most successful retrievals bypass the exchange.
mitigation: Win specific workflows; provide unified audit and budget controls that make fragmented access painful.

failure_mode: Paid source does not improve outcomes
description: The source is licensed and technically accessible but does not measurably improve task success, citation quality, or time saved.
leading_indicator: A/B tests show no uplift or paid calls correlate with more manual review.
mitigation: Pre-register metrics; run shadow tests; drop sources that do not beat baseline after fair evaluation.

description: Buyers will not share prompts, traces, outcomes, or human-review labels, preventing demand graph and uplift proof.
leading_indicator: Security/legal review prohibits storing raw traces or outcome labels.
mitigation: Store normalized metadata, use buyer-owned trace pointers, support private deployment and opt-in aggregation.

description: The exchange brokers personal-data-bearing datasets and becomes a data broker without registration or deletion workflows.
leading_indicator: Catalog expands into people data, news archives, or enrichment data without broker-status analysis.
mitigation: Get legal determination; exclude people-data at launch; build DROP/deletion workflow if required.

failure_mode: GDPR erasure cannot reach caches or embeddings
description: Personal data in cached responses or vector indexes cannot be reliably deleted or corrected.
leading_indicator: Deletion requests require manual engineering or leave orphaned vectors.
mitigation: License-aware cache/index inventory; deletion queue; avoid buyer-hosted embeddings in MVP.

description: The exchange holds buyer balances and pays publishers without a licensed partner or valid exemption.
leading_indicator: Finance design includes prepaid wallet controlled by platform bank account.
mitigation: Use Stripe Connect/Adyen/ACH partner; agent-of-payee structure; payments counsel before launch.

description: A sanctioned or fraudulent buyer/publisher transacts through the marketplace.
leading_indicator: Manual onboarding skips beneficial ownership or continuous screening.
mitigation: KYB/KYC vendor, sanctions screening, geo-blocking, periodic rescreening, immediate suspension.

description: Marketplace facilitator, VAT reverse-charge, or publisher withholding obligations are missed.
leading_indicator: Finance cannot produce tax reports by jurisdiction or publisher status.
mitigation: Use tax engine and payments partner; collect W-8/W-9/VAT IDs; start with limited jurisdictions.

description: Paid placement influences source selection without adequate disclosure, causing buyer and user distrust.
leading_indicator: Buyers ask whether high-ranked sources are sponsored or users complain about ads in answers.
mitigation: Postpone sponsored discovery; disclose material connections; never override quality floors.

description: Agents omit required citations or display them incorrectly, breaching license and undermining publisher trust.
leading_indicator: Publisher audits find missing source names, links, or date/title metadata in buyer UI.
mitigation: Return mandatory citation payloads; sample UI rendering; contractually require display.

description: Model answers distort or overstate licensed source content, making the source appear wrong or misleading.
leading_indicator: Human reviewers find source-supported citations attached to unsupported claims.
mitigation: Grounded-answer verifier, quote boundaries, source snippets, HITL for high-risk tasks, buyer disclaimers.

description: Sensitive buyer prompts, privileged material, PHI, supplier data, or trade secrets are exposed to publishers or logs.
leading_indicator: Logs contain raw prompts or source adapters receive unnecessary context.
mitigation: Data minimization, field-level redaction, tenant isolation, DPA, private deployment for sensitive workflows.

description: A cached source response licensed to one buyer or user is served to another without rights.
leading_indicator: Cache keys omit tenant, user, license, or region scope in review.
mitigation: License-aware cache keys, private cache default, automated tests for cross-user bleed.

description: The exchange continues serving content after license expiration, correction, takedown, or privacy deletion request.
leading_indicator: Revocation requests require manual tickets and no SLA measurement.
mitigation: Revocation service, purge queue, source disable switch, buyer notifications, deletion certificates.

description: A buyer uses many permitted calls to bulk extract or reconstruct a licensed database.
leading_indicator: Query patterns sweep sequential IDs, broad alphabetic ranges, or high catalog fraction.
mitigation: Catalog fraction caps, anomaly detection, per-buyer diversity limits, suspension rights.

description: Billable usage is undercounted, overcounted, duplicated, or disputed, damaging publisher and buyer trust.
leading_indicator: Reconciliation mismatch between exchange ledger and publisher logs exceeds tolerance.
mitigation: Idempotency keys, append-only ledger, weekly reconciliation, refund workflow, independent audit.

failure_mode: Source outage or latency breaks agent workflows
description: Upstream source API is slow or down, making paid routing unusable in real-time agent tasks.
leading_indicator: p95 latency exceeds task budget or source 5xx rate spikes.
mitigation: SLA monitoring, fallback sources, circuit breakers, cache where licensed, buyer-visible status.

description: Source changes schema, pricing, rate limits, or license terms unexpectedly, breaking integrations or margins.
leading_indicator: Source release notes or invoices show unannounced changes.
mitigation: Contract notice periods, adapter versioning, integration tests, price-change alerts, runoff clauses.

failure_mode: Publisher revokes supply after low revenue
description: Publishers leave because payout is too small, buyer identity is hidden, or support burden is high.
leading_indicator: Publisher statements show trivial revenue and rising support tickets.
mitigation: Set expectations, minimum guarantees only where justified, transparent ledgers, focus on high-value workflows.

description: Buyer security, legal, privacy, and procurement review exceeds startup runway or pilot budget.
leading_indicator: Pilot stalls in vendor onboarding for more than 90 days.
mitigation: Use existing marketplaces/partners, limited-scope pilots, buyer-private deployment, standardized security packet.

description: Healthcare, finance, legal, or compliance requirements make each deal services-heavy and low-margin.
leading_indicator: Each buyer requires bespoke DPA, audit, security architecture, and workflow customization.
mitigation: Start with one vertical; productize repeated controls; avoid PHI/market-data heavy cases in MVP.

failure_mode: Accidental PHI or consumer health data exposure
description: Clinical or wellness data enters the system without HIPAA/health-privacy architecture or BAAs.
leading_indicator: Sales pipeline includes health workflows before legal/technical readiness.
mitigation: Exclude PHI at launch; no BAA; dedicated healthcare architecture only if vertical chosen.

description: Exchange mishandles display/non-display or derived-data restrictions from market-data providers.
leading_indicator: Finance source contract references exchange/vendor-of-record audit terms not implemented.
mitigation: Avoid exchange market data initially or implement vendor-grade entitlements and audits.

description: Attackers exfiltrate licensed source responses, embeddings, or transaction data.
leading_indicator: Pen test finds weak tenant isolation, exposed logs, or overly broad admin access.
mitigation: SOC2 roadmap, encryption, least privilege, audit logs, secrets management, incident plan.

description: Major agent hosts restrict external tools, paid calls, or third-party MCP servers, reducing distribution.
leading_indicator: Platform announces connector review, fee, or allowlist requirements.
mitigation: Support REST and cloud/private deployment; diversify distribution channels; comply with host policies.

failure_mode: Dynamic pricing feature creates legal/commercial backlash
description: Algorithmic pricing or surge pricing for sources feels manipulative or violates antitrust/consumer rules.
leading_indicator: Publishers request automated price optimization or buyers complain about opaque price changes.
mitigation: Use transparent publisher-set rate cards; require quote/preauthorization; antitrust review.

failure_mode: Unit economics fail at microtransaction prices
description: Per-call gross margin cannot cover payments, gateway cost, support, compliance, and disputes.
leading_indicator: Gross margin per call is positive before support but negative after operations.
mitigation: Bundle calls, monthly minimums, higher-value verticals, prepaid/invoice billing, kill low-price sources.

description: AI usage payouts are too small relative to publisher expectations, creating churn and negative PR.
leading_indicator: Publishers compare payout to lost traffic or licensing expectations and complain publicly.
mitigation: Avoid inflated promises; provide transparent reports; target sources where per-use value is meaningful.

description: AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks become the preferred procurement and governance layer for AI-ready data.
leading_indicator: Enterprise buyers require listing through existing cloud marketplace before purchase.
mitigation: List through cloud marketplaces; make exchange a vertical control layer rather than separate procurement path.

failure_mode: Regulatory action on ads in answers
description: Sponsored source placement or answer advertising triggers FTC, EU, or state UDAP scrutiny.
leading_indicator: Product ships answer ads or hidden paid source boosts; complaints mention deception.
mitigation: Disclose sponsorship, separate sponsored module, disable for high-risk workflows, legal review.

description: Exchange supports agents using end-user consumer subscriptions against publisher terms, inviting CFAA/contract claims.
leading_indicator: Product roadmap includes browser login or customer credential replay for non-participating publishers.
mitigation: Use publisher-authorized APIs/licenses; entitlement routing only where owner authorization is explicit.

failure_mode: Overbuilt horizontal marketplace before pilot proof
description: Team spends capital on self-serve marketplace, graph ML, sponsored ads, and broad catalog before proving one paid workflow.
leading_indicator: Roadmap prioritizes marketplace UI and growth loops before paid pilot renewal.
mitigation: Build narrow vertical MVP; use manual ops; require decisive kill criteria after 90 days.
